question: When owner-native mechanisms change after a retained research prior was earned, should the prior expire by age/revision, remain unchanged, or be revalidated against the support conditions that originally made each clause true?

naturalCase.oldFinding: Repeated procedure text plus incident provenance did not beat strong current Tool-contract facts on the frozen recovery workload; the Skill candidate was rejected; no Skill repository/runtime/marketplace/registry was authorized; dynamic Skill compilation remained unproven.

postPriorOwnerShift.change: capability composition truth: installed != Run-admitted != turn-admitted, plus exact advanced Tool-surface composition seam

reusable procedural capital: externally evaluated/promoted exact cross-Run procedure references compile into existing cognition seed path; no automatic injection, ranking, repository or Harness-owned evaluator

bounded programmatic Tool composition: one semantic plan -> linear ToolProgram -> same physical Tool effects; repository-repair ablation reduced model calls from 7 to 2 with the same 5 physical Tool calls and existing per-step evidence/UNKNOWN semantics

expireOnAgeOrRevision.reason: Harness revision movement does not falsify the clauses that repeated procedure text alone is insufficient, procedure role is not correctness/Tool authority, or that no Skill registry/runtime is justified. Expiring the whole prior would delete still-supported constraints.

retainPriorUnchanged.reason: The broad wording that capability compilation remains unproven is no longer accurate without qualification: Harness now proves exact reusable procedural-source admission and a bounded mechanical ToolProgram composition with measured model-call reduction. Keeping the old prior as one indivisible statement hides real capability growth.

supportBoundRevalidation.reason: Split the old prior into clauses, identify the mechanism/support assumptions for each, and compare only threatened clauses to owner-native new evidence. This retains still-supported anti-platform/semantic-authority boundaries while narrowing the previously broad negative capability-compilation claim.

clauseDisposition.clause: Repeated procedure text plus provenance is insufficient to become an authoritative reusable Skill when decisive current Tool-contract facts already solve the task.
clauseDisposition.supportCondition: The candidate adds no independent stable decision value beyond exact Tool/caller facts on the target task.
clauseDisposition.basis: Harness P1 still requires external evaluation/promotion and P2 does not turn procedure text into semantic authority.

clauseDisposition.clause: Procedure role does not imply correctness or Tool authority.
clauseDisposition.supportCondition: Semantic promotion and physical action authority remain separate owners.
clauseDisposition.basis: Harness P1 explicitly preserves Procedure role != Correctness and Procedure role != Tool authority; P2 rechecks each inner step against exact current turn tools.

clauseDisposition.clause: No generic Skill repository/runtime/marketplace/registry is authorized.
clauseDisposition.supportCondition: Exact reuse/composition can be expressed with existing owner-owned sources, cognition admission, and Tool/effect substrate.
clauseDisposition.basis: P1 explicitly rejects Harness-owned Skill storage/evaluation/promotion; P2 rejects program registry/scheduler/second effect store.

clauseDisposition.supportCondition: No accepted mechanism has demonstrated reusable cross-Run procedure admission or bounded multi-step mechanical composition with measured benefit.
clauseDisposition.basis: That support condition changed. P1 proves exact externally promoted procedural reuse; P2 proves bounded ToolProgram composition with 7->2 model-call reduction. What remains unproven is generic learned semantic Skill compilation that itself earns decision value across materially different tasks.

clauseDisposition.clause: The P3 recovery Skill candidate itself was not proven useful.
clauseDisposition.supportCondition: Frozen P3 baseline/holdout results remain unchanged.
clauseDisposition.basis: Later Harness capability growth does not rewrite the old experiment outcome.

firstPrinciplesModel.priorForm: K = (claim, mechanism, supportConditions, evidenceFamily, scope, falsifier, negativeTransferBoundary)
firstPrinciplesModel.trigger: Owner/model/task/environment change creates revalidation pressure only when it plausibly threatens a support condition.
firstPrinciplesModel.decision: If no support is threatened, retain. If some support changes, split/narrow the affected clauses. If decisive new evidence contradicts the mechanism, supersede. Historical experiment outcome remains historical even when current applicability changes.
firstPrinciplesModel.ttl: Wall-clock age alone is not a semantic invalidator.
firstPrinciplesModel.revision: Revision movement is a review trigger, not a falsifier.

externalConsistency: This scoped result is consistent with changepoint/distribution-shift and negative-transfer research: old information may require selective tempering/reset after regime change, but the relevant object is changed generating/support structure rather than age alone. External literature is mechanism pressure, not Ordivon authority.
claimBoundary: One natural Ordivon owner shift establishes the usefulness of clause-level support-bound revalidation over all-or-nothing age/revision invalidation in this case. It does not establish an automatic prior engine, generic changepoint detector, TTL, or universal support graph.
nextFalsifier: Find a second materially different earned prior whose support changes because of a model/task/environment shift and where support-bound revalidation predicts a different retained/narrowed/superseded result than both keep-all and expire-all, then test downstream owner-native outcome.
authorityBoundary: Computing research/Knowledge candidate only; no Harness mutation and no automatic cross-Run prior injection or expiry.
